title: Configuration frame during row copying
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, and let $x$ and $y$ be finite Boolean words. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$, let $b$ be a Boolean value, let $n$ assign a natural number to each of the $(1+M.k)+(1+M.k)$ fields, let $record$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $T,t$ be natural numbers. For each index $i$ among the $(1+M.k)+(1+M.k)+1$ row positions and each copier control $q$ among five possibilities, placing the row configuration on the selected tapes of the recorder configuration, with state corresponding to the source state, $b$, and row state $(i,q)$, gives exactly the recorder configuration in that state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $y$
$n$ assigns a natural number to each of the $(1+M.k)+(1+M.k)$ fields
$q$ is one of five copier controls
replaced: For every source configuration, tag, movement counts, record, clock budget, logical time, field index, and copier control, relocating the row-copy seam into the recorder's tapes, retaining every inactive slot from the recorder configuration itself, yields exactly the recorder configuration in the row-copying phase; the inactive bank includes every source cell and head and the unchanged clock.
